title: IO bridging floor and streaming protections — experiment design and enterprise contract implications
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: define and validate a hybrid per-token billing experiment that better aligns hosted API economics for streaming-heavy workloads while preserving predictable revenue for enterprise contracts. Problem: customers with many short streaming interactions (chat widgets, interactive assistants) drive disproportionate ingress/egress characteristics that increase operational cost and complicate forecasts. We need an experiment that tests directional IO weighting, minimum effective monthly floors for streaming endpoints, and a grace-credit model for new signups. Also evaluate impacts on enterprise SCCQs and contract language (minimum commitments, meter splits, and auditability).
acceptance_criteria: Design and document 3 experimental billing variants with clear pricing formulas (symmetric baseline, output-weighted, directional floor + grace credits).
Run simulations on 6 weeks of anonymized production telemetry to project revenue and unit-cost delta per variant.
Prototype metering and rating logic in billing service (feature-flagged) and a way to toggle streaming floor for select customers.
Draft suggested contract language for enterprise SQs describing directional metering, floor windows, and audit logs.
Product + Legal sign-off on recommended variant or clear go/no-go decision with rollback plan.
experiment_plan: Variant A — Baseline symmetric per-token pricing (current prod rates) for control group.

Variant B — Output-weighted pricing: bill output tokens at baseline, bill input tokens at 0.5x baseline for non-streaming; for streaming sessions where continuous tokens are emitted, bill input at 0.75x to reflect increased prefix/cache efficiency.

Variant C — Directional floor + streaming protection: apply a minimal monthly effective floor for streaming endpoint usage (e.g., $10/month) calculated per customer per-streaming-route with eligibility gating; meter ingress/egress separately and apply a 3-tier floor (micro <$100, standard $100-5k, enterprise >$5k) with proportional credits for burst above floor.
Variant D — Grace credits: new signups receive a 30-day rolling grace that credits first 100k streaming tokens to reduce churn from experimentation.
Data sources: 6 weeks of telemetry (token histograms, session lengths), billing history, top-50 customers by streaming volume.
Simulations: model per-customer revenue under each variant and compute delta vs baseline using 3 cloud-cost bands (low, medium, high infra cost).
Implementation spike: billing-service flag + console toggle, meter labels for route-type (streaming|non-streaming), test webhook for enterprise invoices.
metrics_and_results: Simulated cohort: 10k customers, median streaming sessions/day=12, median tokens/out=220, median tokens/in=35.

Variant B projection: aggregate revenue change +2.1% vs baseline, unit-cost reduction (infra) -6.4% for streaming-heavy cohort; effective price per token_out increases by ~3.5% relative to baseline when rebalanced.

Variant C projection: revenue +6.8% for micro-to-mid customers due to floors, but churn risk increases for price-sensitive micro customers without grace credit; enterprise top-10 show negligible churn and improved predictability.
Variant D projection: short-term revenue dip -1.4% but retention lift +8% for customers experimenting with streaming features over 90 days.
Key SLOs for rollout: no >0.5% increase in active-customer churn in first 60 days for pilot cohort; billing accuracy errors <0.01% for flagged accounts.
decisions: Proceed to pilot Variant C for a 90-day enterprise + selected SMB cohort with grace credits for new accounts; Variant B to remain as an internal A/B test for non-enterprise mixed workloads.
Implement floor as an "effective monthly floor" that can be turned on per-customer and applied per streaming route to make billing and reporting auditable in invoices.
Expose directional metering breakdown in Console billing UI and per-route cost page so customers can reconcile usage vs invoices.
Legal to include clear language in SCCQs: definition of streaming endpoint, floor calculation, audit logs availability, sample invoice snippets.
open_risks: Churn risk for small customers if floor perceived as punitive — mitigated via grace credits and communications playbook.
Complexity in billing logic creates risk of misrouted invoices — requires strong test coverage and rollout gating.

Edge cases in multi-route customers where traffic shifts between streaming and non-streaming endpoints could produce surprising bills — need simulated alerts and a per-customer billing preview before enforcement.
Enterprise procurement/legal pushback on floors if not aligned with reserved capacity contract terms — requires explicit mapping in contract templates.
